findings.title: Cleanup on a failed `BenchmarkSandbox.__enter__` is unspecified
findings.description:
Environment resolution (step 4 of the `__enter__` flow) is the step most likely to fail. D5 and the Risk section both expect historical locks to stop resolving. By that point `HistoryFreeSandbox` has already created the lock and tree, and `ScrubbedEnvironment` has created `<id>.home/`. Python does not call `__exit__` when `__enter__` raises. The State Management section says the four directories are removed on exit, and the orphan sweep only handles dead owners.

The slice does not say that a failure inside `__enter__` unwinds what steps 1 to 3 created. 422 will probably qualify many candidates in one process. If a failure leaves its tree, `.venv` and lock behind, they pile up until that process ends. Walkthrough step 5 also expects "no `.venv` created" after a failure. A partial install can violate that, because `--locked` rejects a stale lock before installing but not a download that fails midway.

Fix: state that `__enter__` removes everything it created before it re-raises `SandboxError` or `EnvironmentResolutionError`. Add a test that asserts nothing is left under `~/.config/squadron/benchmark/` after an install failure and after an install timeout.

findings.title: `reference_sha` and `project_id` are added to case identity, which the architecture does not list
findings.description: The architecture says a case is identified by "start commit, task text, hidden and superseded test sets, grader commands". D1 adds `project_id`, `kind`, `reference_sha`, `hidden_fixtures` and `excluded_tests`. The `excluded_tests` field is consistent with the keystone slice's exclusion list. `reference_sha` is a sound addition, because hidden test source is read from the reference at grading time. The slice states the deviation, but 420-arch's immutability principle still reads as the narrower list. Update the architecture sentence so later slices (425 and 426) do not work from the older definition.

findings.title: Mock-patch classification is checked only on Python 3.13
findings.description: The reporter plugin runs under the start commit's own interpreter, which can be older than 3.13. It also reads `unittest.mock._patch` internals. D11 says the behavior was "Checked on Python 3.13" and says nothing about other versions. If the introspection fails on another version, the failure falls through to `other_exception`. That is the safe direction, because 422 excludes it as undecidable, and it matches the architecture's rule that a check which cannot decide must exclude the case. The cost is lower fix-case yield from false exclusions. Record this direction explicitly. Also run the mock-target fixture test on more than one interpreter version, or state which versions are supported.

findings.title: Frontmatter omits 400
findings.description: The slice consumes `SourceLanguage` from 400's `metrology/snapshot_models.py`. It also mirrors 400's registry keying and in-tree `.venv` layout, and aligns its `lockfile_sha256` name with 400's. The body lists this under Interfaces Required, but `dependencies: [420, 177, 320]` leaves out 400. Add it so the dependency graph matches the body.
